clue.text: Rifle a London suburb

definitions.meaning: the standard British army rifle, named after the town where it was made
a borough on the northern edge of Greater London

explanation.surface: Instructions to raid a commuter district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' reads as a verb (ransack), but it is the noun, the gun named after its place of manufacture.
explanation.definitionFit: The same place name serves both: the suburb, and the service weapon first made at its small-arms factory.

clue.text: Urge winner to get whiskers cut short!

definitions.note: the plural shortened by its final letter gives a whisker, one thing that whisks

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
one who beats another wins

explanation.surface: Telling a champion to get a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whiskers' looks like facial hair; dropping its final letter gives a kitchen tool that whisks.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool for whisking eggs and cream.

clue.text: Fussy decoration on pinnacle, round top of clerestory

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the ornament is placed around the letter

parts.note: a finial is the ornament at the top of a spire or pinnacle

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of clerestory

explanation.surface: A fussy ornament on a pinnacle near the top of a church's upper wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives C, and 'round' puts FINIAL around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for finicky, overparticular.

clue.text: Bugle call may come as this sort of surprise

definitions.text: Bugle call may come as this sort of surprise

parts.words: Bugle call may come as this sort of surprise
parts.note: reveille wakes sleepers, literally making them look; figuratively a startling revelation

explanation.surface: A trumpet blast could startle you.
explanation.walkthrough: The morning bugle literally gets sleepers to look up; the phrase is also a revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that is startling, which forces you to see things clearly.

clue.text: A peach is food, of course

definitions.meaning: slang for an attractive person
a course of a meal, prepared food

explanation.surface: A peach is naturally something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but it means one course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a good-looking person and a prepared item served in a meal.

clue.text: Blueprints for king and other pieces

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

indicators.note: other here means made different, so the letters of pieces are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plans drawn up for the king piece and the rest of the chessmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' looks like 'the remaining', but it is the anagram signal on the word that follows it; 'for' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sets of detailed instructions for producing something, one for a dish, one for a building or machine.

clue.text: Showing up to rout a right-winger

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a large party or revel
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: Arriving to defeat a conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rout' looks like a defeat, but it is the old sense of a riotous party. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing or exposing something, as a disclosure does.

clue.text: Surrounded by US agents, let's say, you are also caught

annotationWithheld.why: Surrounded by US agents, let's say, you are also caught (5): CIA round UR gives CURIA, but the page prints 'also caught', and nothing there defines a papal court
annotationWithheld.clue: Surrounded by US agents, let's say, you are also caught

clue.text: Crashed like Pelion

definitions.meaning: of cars, collided in a heap
in myth the giants heaped Mount Pelion on top of Ossa to reach heaven

explanation.surface: A pile-up compared to a Greek mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The giants put Pelion upon Ossa in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles in a multiple crash are stacked together, as mountains in the myth were stacked one on another.

clue.text: As a speaker, Dorothy missed the last point

indicators.note: missed the last means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: Dorothy L Sayers, detective novelist
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark about Dorothy's speech lacking a final point.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey novels.
explanation.definitionFit: One who says something, an utterer.

clue.text: Spirit — it sounds like gin

definitions.meaning: a supernatural being of Arabian tales, granting wishes
the Arabic word for such a being, jinn (also spelt djinn), is pronounced like the drink gin

explanation.surface: A remark that a ghostly being has a name pronounced like a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts toward drink, which 'gin' reinforces; the second half points instead to the Arabic word jinn, from which this spirit's English name is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A magical being from Arabian folklore, such as the one in Aladdin's lamp, is this kind of spirit.

clue.text: Continually hemmed in, make a dash for it, one by one

indicators.note: hemmed in means surrounded, so one word is placed inside another

parts.note: a sally is a sudden rush out, a sortie
ever means always or continually

explanation.surface: Someone constantly boxed in who makes a run for it, individually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a dash for it' reads as escaping, but it is the military sense of a sortie out of a besieged place.
explanation.definitionFit: Separately or individually, each in turn, is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Cut out old church exercise

parts.note: ex means former or old
CE is the Church of England
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Old church drill has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to exclude or leave out, which is what cutting out does.

clue.text: Priestess of Venus might have called this a shrub

definitions.text: Priestess of Venus might have called this
definitions.meaning: Hero, priestess of Venus, might have cried '...!' to her lover who swam the Hellespont to reach her
a poisonous evergreen with pink or white flowers

explanation.surface: A remark that a priestess of the goddess of love might have named a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Greek myth Hero, a priestess of Venus (Aphrodite), waited for Leander each night; her cry to him, O plus his name, runs together as the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean flowering evergreen bush, also called rosebay.

clue.text: Novelty introduced in pub gets enthusiastic reception

indicators.note: gets means the pub is followed by the applause

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is warm applause

explanation.surface: Something new at the local is warmly applauded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something new and original, such as a new method or invention.

clue.text: Bit of bird's-foot found in central Catalonia

indicators.note: found in the central part of the word means the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: A piece of a bird's foot turns up in the middle of Catalonia.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw is one part of a bird of prey's foot.

clue.text: Return of theatre mimic to north offers something to write on

indicators.note: return means the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: A repertory company's impressionist heading north provides stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns the whole string REPAPETON round.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper, for letters, is what you write on.

clue.text: Gentle old foreigner?

definitions.meaning: the falcon-gentle is a female falcon of this species
an archaic word for a stranger or traveller from abroad

explanation.surface: A mild elderly stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentle' looks like an adjective; it is falconry's noun for a female falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon species whose name comes from Latin for wandering, and so also an old word for a pilgrim or alien.

clue.text: Reformed, so deal with crime cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly means roughly treated, so the letters of deal and crime are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reformed is told to treat crime harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' scrambles DEALCRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought back to a good way of life, redeemed.

clue.text: River rose, overturning tank

indicators.note: overturning means upsetting, so the letters of river and rose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A river in flood capsizes an army tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' looks like the action of the flood on the tank, but it scrambles RIVERROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large storage tank or lake for water is this.

clue.text: What if saucy girl covers pages with tar?

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the girl's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Sue, a girl's name
OS, an ordinary seaman, is a sailor or tar

explanation.surface: Wondering what happens if a cheeky girl smears tar on pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like pitch spread over the pages, but it is an old word for a sailor; 'saucy' only colours the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Let us imagine is the sense of the verb, a hypothetical.

clue.text: Widow robbed of last letter as souvenir

indicators.note: robbed of means losing, and the letter lost is the final one of the word for widow

parts.note: relict is an old word for a widow

explanation.surface: A widow stripped of her final letter as a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or memento of the past.

clue.text: Taking part in play involving God and crown

indicators.note: and joins the god to the monarch

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god
the crown stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: Acting in a drama about a deity and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lares were the household gods of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Larking is playing about, fooling around.

clue.text: Old parrot that pestered young Percy

definitions.meaning: an old name for a parrot
in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1, Harry Percy (Hotspur) complains of a perfumed courtier, calling him this, who pestered him after battle

explanation.surface: An ancient bird that bothered a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Percy is Hotspur, who in Henry IV Part 1 describes being pestered by a dandified lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for a parrot later came to mean a vain, chattering dandy.

clue.text: Squeeze into cupboard

definitions.meaning: to push hard
a large cupboard, as a linen cupboard

explanation.surface: Cramming something into a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To push or compress, and an old word for a shelved wall cupboard.

clue.text: Bond put up willingly covering leader of expedition

indicators.note: covering in a down clue means placed above
put up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: as soon means as willingly, 'I'd as soon'

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A pact willingly backing an expedition's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses SOON; 'covering' puts it above E from 'leader of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope that binds, a tie.

clue.text: I agree to a new patroness

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of I agree are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone consenting to a new sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IAGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria, the nymph who advised King Numa of Rome, gives her name to a female adviser or patron.

clue.text: Way to record action

definitions.meaning: a means or method
a measure taken, as to take this

explanation.surface: A method for recording something done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to record' is a link phrase between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A means to an end, and a measure or action taken.

clue.text: Smith for one makes periodical appearances

definitions.meaning: Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations, is an example
a weekly news magazine of this name comes out regularly

explanation.surface: A man called Smith shows up from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' seems an ordinary surname, but it is Adam Smith; 'periodical' is the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Smith is a founding figure of the discipline, and the London weekly magazine of the same name appears every week.

clue.text: On impulse, Mona exhibits peculiar expression

parts.note: the id is the instinctive impulses in Freudian psychology
Mona is the Latin name for the Isle of Man, IOM

explanation.surface: On a whim, the Mona Lisa shows an odd look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mona' suggests the Mona Lisa's smile; it is the Roman name for the Isle of Man. 'On' and 'exhibits' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase peculiar to a language, whose meaning is not the sum of its words.

clue.text: Observed ambassador and bishop inside speakeasy

indicators.note: inside places the ambassador and bishop within the word for observed

parts.note: seen means observed
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An envoy and a bishop were spotted in an illegal bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts HEB within SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish word for an unlicensed drinking den, the same as an illegal bar during Prohibition.

clue.text: Left with uncle as promised

definitions.meaning: uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, so goods left with him are pawned
vowed or given one's word

explanation.surface: Something left with a relative, as agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawned goods are given as security, and a vow is a solemn undertaking, both senses of giving something as surety.
